question.text: The concentration of fluoride, lead, nitrate and iron in a water sample from an underground lake was found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1000</mn><mo> </mo><mi>ppb</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>ppb</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>ppm</mi><mo> </mo><mi>and</mi><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi>ppm</mi></math>, respectively. This water is unsuitable for drinking due to high concentration of:

solution.text:
Parameters                           Maximum prescribed concentration in  drinking water                                                                        

Iron                                         0.2 ppm

Fluroide                                  1.5 ppm

Lead                                        50 ppb

Nitrate                                     50 ppm

Hence the concentration of nitrate in a given
water sample exceeds from the upper limit as
given above.
